_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: Show original Speech-list frequencies and place reference views beside desktop cards
detail: Restored released-word frequency values from the pinned EsPal, Lexique, Portuguese FrequencyWords, and Czech FrequencyWords source lists, with source and unit recorded for every language.
Merged-lemma cards now sum those source-listed form frequencies for their front-of-card figure; harvested example sentences no longer supply a misleading per-million number.
Spanish and French use per-million rates. Portuguese and Czech show source-list occurrence counts because those published lists do not provide a per-million denominator.
On wide desktop screens, Find a word, lyric breakdown, and card knowledge open to the right of the visible card; smaller screens keep the existing sheet layout.

entries.summary: Conjugation mode: the off-model pattern no longer calls itself one-offs while listing the verbs that share it
detail: Forms whose ending does not match the model at all were labelled no shared pattern, one-offs, and then immediately listed three other verbs that behave the same way. They are off the model, not one-offs, and the chip now says so.

entries.summary: Conjugation mode: a separate drill page for verb patterns, reached from the conjugate drawer on the back of a card
detail: The conjugate drawer now has a Drill this verb in conjugation mode button above the external paradigm link. That link is the only way in, so the new page and the study app can be worked on without treading on each other. It appears only for languages that have a deck built; Spanish has one today.
Conjugation mode is its own page at /conjugation/, sharing no HTML, CSS or JS with the study app. Choose what you want to drill, drill it, or look up a full paradigm.

Choose has eight collapsed sections, each showing its own current selection on the right, so the whole menu of options is readable on a phone without opening anything: tenses, verb type, patterns, repetition, how common, persons, prompt direction, provenance.

Verb type (regular, spelling change, stem change, irregular) is recomputed against the tenses you picked, so tener counts as irregular when the present is selected and regular when only the imperfect is.
Patterns lists every stem alternation found in the data with example verbs, so you can drill just the o-ue group or just the one-offs.

Repetition offers one card per lesson: the present indicative of the 193 commonest verbs is 1,154 forms but only 53 distinct lessons, and coverage mode shows each lesson once, taught by a verb picked at random from the verbs that share it.

The drill has no buttons. Space or tap reveals, space again advances, left arrow goes back, swipe moves, and t opens the full table on the tense you just missed. The answer names the pattern and the verbs that share it.
Prompt direction can be flipped to show the English meaning instead of the infinitive.
Tables takes a verb by search and one tense from a dropdown, rather than listing every tense at once.
Nothing is scored, stored or scheduled yet. This is the selection layer only.

How the patterns are worked out: for each form the builder takes the commonest ending for verbs of that class in that tense and person, strips it, and records the minimal edit from the infinitive's stem to the stem actually used. pens to piens is e-ie; busc to busqu is c-qu. Two forms are the same lesson when class, tense, person, ending and that edit all match. No verb is hand-tagged, and the same code runs for Portuguese, French and Czech.
Service worker cache bumped to flashcards-v496; style.css and light-theme.css version tags bumped.

entries.summary: Give card grammar labels a steady layout and make setup controls clearer
detail: Reserved consistent capsule layouts for one, two, three, and larger POS and lemma groups, with shared font fitting for long labels.
Added breathing room around desktop card content while keeping the phone layout compact.
Grouped account, tutorial, and settings controls on the right of the setup bar and made language a clearer two-line button on the left.
Centred the Choose level and Your next set headings and made each heading and its information icon one help button.

entries.summary: Show sense commonness once and let learners mark rarer senses deliberately
detail: Removed the repeated commonness bar from a collapsed sense heading when it contains only one visible subrow.
Added an opt-in rarer-senses section to the knowledge menu and an entry point on the Rarer uses page.
Saved explicit rare-sense Known or Review choices as stable item progress; rare Review can return in focused review without marking the whole word known.

entries.summary: The tutorial now opens by walking through the real setup screen, and Lyrics mode gets a slide of its own instead of appearing unannounced
detail: The intro is no longer three tick-boxes filling themselves in. It is a replica of the setup screen you actually use, and a pointer moves through it: pick a language, pick whether you want everyday speech or song lyrics, pick a level, pick a set. Each choice holds long enough to read before the next one.
It ends on a live Learn 20 new cards button and waits. You open the first card yourself.

The order is now front of the card, back of the card, then a slide explaining what Lyrics mode is, then a Lyrics card. Previously the deck changed silently and the Lyrics card had to explain itself in its own annotations.

The Lyrics slide says the three things that are actually different: the example is a real lyric, you can play it in Spotify, and the number counts that artist's lines rather than the language at large.
Removed the Speech and Lyrics labels from the header and the step counter. They named two modes before you had met either one.
Underneath, the walkthrough is now a plain list of steps rather than two decks with two faces each, so the order of the story is one list to read and to change.

entries.summary: The Fast Track details page now uses the width of the window, states each count once, and no longer reports a verified zero it never counted
detail: The page was capped at 1040px and stacked each explanation above its own controls, so it read as a thin ribbon down the middle of a wide window while the prose wrapped into a narrow column. It now runs to 1480px, and inside each card the explanation sits beside the example and the controls rather than above them, which spends the spare width and cuts the height roughly in half. Below 1180px the card stacks again; below 420px the two cards stack.

Each count appeared twice -- once on the button as '(2707)' and again underneath as '2,707 flashcards merged' -- in two wordings written by two different functions. The info lines are gone. The button carries the figure and says what it is: 'View 2,707 merged forms'.

'View skipped words (0)' is fixed. A zero could mean the vocabulary had not loaded yet, and the button announced it as a counted result. Nothing is now claimed until the words have actually been counted; when they have been and none matched, the page says so in a sentence instead of showing an empty button.
Spanish does have a cognate map -- 4,915 of its 6,000 Speech words carry a score and 1,128 clear the shipped cutoff. The zero came from the map not being in memory yet at the moment the page counted.

Fixed the underlying race: an in-flight cognate-map fetch was not keyed by language, so switching language could make the second language join the first one's load and then record itself as loaded with no scores attached.

entries.summary: Tutorial fixes: a slower setup intro you dismiss yourself, plainer wording, the lemma back on the front, and no more numbered badges
detail: The setup preview now holds on each step long enough to read, and stops on the last one with a live Start set button. You open the first card yourself instead of it racing past. Skip intro still leaves at any point.
The front of a card says Frequency: 21,340/million instead of 'Frequency from the Spanish release', which told you nothing. Same wording and same figures as a real card.
The part-of-speech pill carries its lemma again, so a Portuguese card shows 'verb ter' above the form tem, the way the live card does.
Front of the card and back of the card, not question side and answer side.
Removed the numbered circles on the card and in the notes. They indexed a numbered list that the guided tour had already replaced. The element being explained is outlined in amber instead.

entries.summary: The card tutorial now opens on the question side, plays a short setup intro, and stops repeating itself on Lyrics
detail: A three-step setup preview (language, level, study set) plays for about three seconds before the first card, so the walkthrough starts where you would really start. Tap it or press Skip intro to go straight to the card.
Every chapter now shows the question side first and flips to the answer side, matching the order you meet cards when studying.
The card no longer flips when you tap it or press space. Only Continue and the mobile Next/Back buttons turn it, so the tour cannot get out of step. Left and right arrows still jump chapters.
The Lyrics chapter only annotates what is actually different: the translation, the song credit, Spotify playback, the example dots, and the lyric line count. The tutorial is 17 steps instead of 26.
Fixed the step counter, which was counting the wrong face and showing the wrong number on every question side.

entries.summary: Clarify sense grouping and commonness on cards
detail: Grouped matching two-sense entries, including no/not negation, when they share a context.
Showed compact commonness bars on every collapsed sense group in label mode and used one high-contrast bar colour.
Kept long surface and lemma pairs on one line by fitting their measured widths.

entries.summary: Clarify language and music choices and group skipped-word decks by level
detail: Made language, mode, and music-source choices a clearer sequence with consistent descriptions and Back navigation.
Grouped skipped Fast Track word decks beneath their original levels, in sets of up to 20, with existing card progress on each set.
Kept merged word forms as a note on their shared cards and clarified the empty skipped-deck state.

entries.summary: Make home controls easier to use and clarify review and source icons
detail: Enlarged the top bar, language control, main actions, and set targets; sets now show five per row.
Moved review cards into their own section above skipped Fast Track words and removed the level-suggestion skip control.
Grouped level and set information, simplified Fast Track to its toggle and Details action, and replaced fuzzy source favicons with larger vector marks.

entries.summary: Rename the tile to Rarer uses and link matching dictionary senses
detail: The tile and page now say Rarer uses: senses that show up less often in speech.
Dictionary senses that share an exact gloss or context are grouped, with a small pager when they are otherwise the same shade.

entries.summary: Tighten Other uses, the set scrubber, and skipped Fast Track decks
detail: Rare/other uses now group matching glosses under part-of-speech headings, scroll inside the card, and use the page subtitle to explain they are less common than Uncommon.
The active-set scrubber and settings icon no longer sit in boxes; return-to text still appears on child cards.
Fast Track on the setup page is skipped-word decks of 20, started from small numbered pills.

entries.summary: Show the actual lemma beside each merged word form
detail: Merged form lists show the lemma and its matching translation on the left, with the skipped form and its translation on the right.
The surviving card surface is no longer mistaken for the lemma when it is another inflection.

entries.summary: Fix Rare Sense button opening the card
detail: Moved the part-of-speech label formatter into shared scope so rare dictionary senses render without an error.
Updated app asset versions and the service worker cache to deliver the fix to existing installations.

entries.summary: Deploy Spanish (6k), Portuguese (6k), and Czech (4k) V14 speech decks
detail: Updated speech decks to signed-off v14 with MWE routing.
Deterministic invariant MWE bypass (no 2-way competition) for fixed grammatical locutions.
Ambiguous MWE competition with active_selection_projection: mwe_augmented and dual-written word leaf.
Exact-text embedding caches expanded and verified for Spanish, Portuguese, and Czech.

entries.summary: Align the back lemma chip to the letterforms, not the font em-box
detail: The lemma chip now centres on the surface's cap-height band so it no longer sits low against the word.

entries.summary: Centre the back lemma chip on the headword, colour it by POS, and fold pronominal se into the chip
detail: Back lemma chip is vertically centred with the surface form and uses the active part-of-speech colour.
Pronominal cards no longer drop 'verb with se' onto a second line; se sits inside the lemma chip on the same row.

entries.summary: Keep the coloured POS pill as the icon, drop italics, and put a small quiet lemma chip beside the back headword
detail: Front capsule again uses the real POS pill on the left, with the lemma as a roman label on the right.
Back title is the large surface plus a compact lemma chip — no filled green capsule and no extra vertical bulk.
Lemma text is no longer italic on either face.

entries.summary: Keep the coloured POS pill as the icon, drop italics, and put a small quiet lemma chip beside the back headword
detail: Front capsule again uses the real POS pill on the left, with the lemma as a roman label on the right.
Back title is the large surface plus a compact lemma chip — no filled green capsule and no extra vertical bulk.
Lemma text is no longer italic on either face.

entries.summary: POS-then-lemma nested pill on the card front, and the same compound object on the back with surface then lemma
detail: Front grammar capsule now reads part of speech first, with the lemma in the inner chip on the right, because POS governs the lemma.
Back headword no longer appends the lemma in brackets; an inflected surface and its dictionary form share one nested pill, surface on the left and lemma on the right.
Cards whose surface already is the lemma keep a plain headword, so infinitives and identical forms are not wrapped in an empty compound chip.

entries.summary: Developer deploy audit card with agent & timestamp, Bad Bunny & Rosalía level resolution, and rare senses button fix
detail: Added top-level deploy audit hero card to the Developer tab showing exact change timestamp, authoring LLM agent, human summary in normal text font, and live Service Worker cache status.
Fixed Bad Bunny and Rosalía zero levels bug in lyrics artist mode by removing shadowing module-level activeArtist variable.
Fixed rare senses toggle button clickability by eliminating illegal nested button in section header.
Added strict instructions to CLAUDE.md and WORKING_WITH_JOSH.md requiring all agents to record exact datetime, agent name, and human summary in dev_changelog.json before deploying.

entries.summary: Sense row audit: fixed blank subsense dashes and improved context visibility across CS, PT, and ES
detail: Subsense cells now show metadata pills (grammar, construction, functional relation) even when the row is unselected, instead of a blank em dash.
Preserved real Wiktionary context (e.g. 'myself', 'himself', 'being a part of') that was previously blanket-wiped when the provider context matched the cleaned context.
Functional metadata (purpose, material, origin, direction) now scores high enough to serve as a sense differentiator.
Fixed grouped text sizing: density calculation evaluates worst-case single row instead of summing all rows, upgrading ~1,100 groups to larger font classes.
Blank dashes dropped from 100% to <2% in CS and PT, and to 0% in ES.

entries.summary: Unified Rare Senses & Expressions child card and retired raw example sentence shards
detail: Combined rare dictionary senses and attached multi-word expressions/locutions into a single unified child card with dedicated badges (PHRASE and amber RARE), POS tags, translations, contexts, and canonical examples.
Added on-demand trigger button ('Explore rare senses & expressions →') at the bottom of the card back, with preserved flip navigation on return.
Replaced the obsolete 'More sentences' toggle with 'Rare senses & expressions' in study preferences after a correct card.
Retired un-disambiguated backup sentence shards in favour of verified WSD-assigned occurrences.

entries.summary: Redo set filtering, SRS spacing penalty, smoother card flips/swipes, 7s auto-continue, and larger provenance icons
detail: Updated Redo Set to only redo cards that were missed or skipped in the set, plus any cards that became due for spaced review if time elapsed.
Added SRS premature recall protection: correct answers within 4 hours of a prior exposure do not advance SRS past stage 1, preventing working-memory recall from inflating multi-day review intervals.
Increased deck completion auto-continue hold delay from 5s to 7s.
Modernized card 3D flip easing and swipe gesture thresholds to prevent glitchy transitions and accidental swipes.
Increased dictionary provenance and source icons to 28px for clearer readability.

entries.summary: Deploy ES V12 deck (es-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Fixed Daily Review loading screen lockup and redesigned Fast Track modal
detail: Fixed full-screen loading screen remaining visible after deck initialization by adding guaranteed dismiss handlers to startDailyReview, next-daily-review, and loadVocabularyData.
Redesigned Fast Track modal with a space-efficient flex layout, bounded height, sticky header/search, and internal smooth scrolling so it never overflows or clips off-screen.

entries.summary: Deploy CS V12 deck (cs-speech-v12-4000x10)
detail: 4,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Deploy ES V12 deck (es-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Deploy PT V12 deck (pt-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Deploy PT V12 deck (pt-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Urgency-scored review queue, 100-card daily batches, and sectioned Review Hub
detail: Continuous needfulness score and urgency tiers (Never Mastered, Critical Lapses, Routine Due) derived directly from the SRS schedule and personal error history.
Review queue prioritizes never-mastered cards and severe lapses first, breaking ties by high-frequency word rank so core vocabulary is refreshed ahead of rare words.
Redesigned the setup Review Hub with one-tap tier slices and 100-card daily batches, with a seamless 'Review Next 100' continuation flow on completion.
Optimized review deck loading with an instant fast path, slashing launch time from ~10s to instantaneous (< 30ms) by avoiding full dictionary scans.

entries.summary: Fast Track setup bar streamlined to compact single-row card and modal opening fixed
detail: Fixed Fast Track words modal not opening when clicking 'Browse words' by removing the overriding inline style on #extrasModal.
Eliminated double nested card borders and duplicate header text from the setup screen, reducing the Fast Track bar to a sleek, compact single-row summary.
Added one-tap card clickability and a direct Fast Track settings shortcut when no words are skipped.

entries.summary: Cognate form scoring upgraded with Jaro-Winkler prefix-weighted similarity
detail: Upgraded form similarity scoring to take the best of normalized Levenshtein and Jaro-Winkler, resolving the suffix penalty that kept transparent citation forms (e.g. Spanish 'abandonar', 'comunicar') below threshold while inflections passed.
Cleaned redundant vowel diacritics from Spanish and Portuguese cognate skeleton configs, relying on Unicode NFD strip_accents.
Rebuilt and deployed Spanish-English cognates mapping (31,828 scored surfaces) to workspace and app.

entries.summary: Adaptive spaced repetition, sticky sense-level exceptions, and global daily review
detail: Intervals adapt to learner failure history with soft drops on mistake (down 2 stages instead of resetting to day 0) and graduation to 365 days.

Sense-level knowledge marking in the card modal now treats unmarked senses as known when marking an exception, makes explicit 'No' sticky against whole-card swipes, and adds a Save & Next Card action.
A level-agnostic Daily Review banner on setup provides 1-tap review for all due cards in the language, and dead CEFR fallback paths are removed.

entries.summary: Speech and Lyrics now share saved progress, with an honest Spotify indicator
detail: Equivalent Speech and Lyrics cards now share historical progress by language and displayed word, while preserving existing saved records.
New answers use the latest review state and continue syncing through the deployed progress service across desktop and mobile.
Spotify shows a circular music visualizer only after playback is confirmed; a button press or pending mobile handoff no longer looks like audio is already playing.

entries.summary: Mobile Spotify playback no longer depends on an already-playing phone app
detail: Mobile Lyrics cards now create a Spotify Web Playback device in the browser instead of requiring Spotify Connect to find an active phone session.
The Spotify button activates browser audio directly from the learner's tap, including the user-gesture bridge required by iOS autoplay rules.
Spotify Connect remains available as a fallback when the browser player cannot become ready; Spotify Premium is still required.

entries.summary: Light mode keeps primary study actions readable
detail: The Learn new cards action keeps its filled accent background instead of becoming white with white text.
The correction applies to the shared responsive control, so the action remains legible on desktop and mobile.
Unstarted set choices retain their intended pale light-mode treatment.

entries.summary: Cross-device progress now loads in the deployed app
detail: The live static configuration now includes the public Google Sheets sync endpoint instead of relying on an excluded backend file.
A phone or other new browser can load the same named learner's historical card, knowledge-item, estimate and completed-level progress.
Static deployment validation now rejects builds that omit either progress sync or Spotify's public OAuth client configuration.

entries.summary: Spotify buttons now open sign-in reliably in deployed Lyrics decks
detail: The public Spotify OAuth client ID now ships with static deployments while private backend configuration remains excluded.
Desktop sign-in opens before asynchronous PKCE work can trigger popup blocking, with a full-page fallback; mobile keeps its full-page return-to-card flow.
The Web Playback SDK now loads only after its readiness callback exists, removing a startup race, and missing configuration produces a visible message instead of a silent no-op.

entries.summary: Example credits now favour readable titles over source codes
detail: Resolved film and television names remain clickable without appending their raw IMDb identifier.
Subtitle line numbers remain in raw Card Data for auditing but no longer clutter learner-facing source credits.
An IMDb identifier is shown only when no human title can be resolved.

entries.summary: Speech examples once again identify their film or television source
detail: Fresh release metadata is normalized into the app's provenance view, restoring IMDb links and subtitle line numbers.
A pinned IMDb title layer adds human movie names and resolves television episodes to their parent series.
The active 2,000-card Spanish release has IMDb links for all 5,997 examples and human titles for 5,967 of them.

entries.summary: POS pills now preserve complete grammatical labels
detail: The fixed front-and-back grammar bay is wide enough for two full labels per row, including Adjective and other longer names.
POS text no longer wraps inside a pill.

entries.summary: The POS grid now occupies the same header position on both card faces
detail: The front-face grammar bay has moved from beside the central surface prompt to the fixed top-right header area used on the back.
Its bounded one-row or two-row layout is unchanged.

entries.summary: Part-of-speech labels now use a stable one- or two-row card layout
detail: One or two labels remain together on one centred row, while three or four labels use a compact two-row grid.
The same bounded grammar area is used on both card faces and remains vertically aligned with the headword.
Every label stays readable, the active part of speech remains highlighted, and changing senses does not reorder the labels.

entries.summary: Assigned cards now show only learner-supported senses and honest percentages
detail: Unused dictionary alternatives remain available as audit-only menu evidence instead of appearing as a giant unassigned learner row.
Assigned sense percentages once again total 100%; the hidden remainder bucket can no longer halve them to 50%.
The explicit unassigned fallback remains available for cards that genuinely have no assigned sense.

entries.summary: Multi-headword card backs no longer repeat lemma labels
detail: Each lemma remains visible in its existing part-of-speech and headword row.
Redundant horizontal lemma strips above the corresponding sense rows were removed.
Sense grouping, selection highlighting and source order are unchanged.

entries.summary: The active workspace now has two explicit demonstration decks
detail: French Speech keeps its fresh 200-card Tatoeba release, while Spanish Lyrics keeps a self-contained Bad Bunny-only release.
Spanish Speech and French Lyrics now say they are awaiting a fresh run instead of attempting to load archived evidence.
All other migration runs, source copies, previews and candidates were moved into a dated recoverable archive outside the live workspace.

entries.summary: Artist acceptance now covers French Lyrics, offline decks and playlist restoration
detail: French Lyrics is available from the language-first chooser and opens its real Artist source without loading Speech first.
An explicitly downloaded immutable Lyrics release can launch offline while the active catalogue remains network-authoritative whenever a connection exists.
A fresh named login now restores its saved cross-artist playlist from SongSets, including contributing-artist provenance.

entries.summary: Language choice now leads directly to a lightweight Speech or Lyrics decision
detail: Choosing Spanish no longer loads the Speech release before a learner can select Lyrics; the exact source starts loading only after it is chosen.
Merge Lemmas remains available as learner-facing form grouping, while optional Lyrics, cognate and morphology controls follow explicit language or release capabilities.
Card backs omit a redundant single inert POS label, cognate settings use clearer Include/Exclude wording, and secondary setup guidance is quieter and provenance-accurate.

entries.summary: Preserved Artist assignments are now clearly identified while auditing
detail: Card Data names the exact immutable Lyrics release supplying the active deck.
Historical prompt IDs that are not part of the new registry are labelled retained assignments instead of unregistered models.
Existing example-level method, translation, song and raw-record evidence remains available while clean WSD regeneration stays optional.

entries.summary: Artist data now stays bound to one immutable release
detail: The active Lyrics catalog rewrites vocabulary, examples, songs, artwork and Spotify data to release-versioned URLs before they are loaded.
Offline caches can retain immutable release assets without accidentally serving data from an older active release.
Preview and active releases now use the same loading path; release activation remains an explicit separate action.

entries.summary: Repeated audit flags now remain separate, traceable events
detail: Every flag gesture has an immutable FlagId, so retries deduplicate safely without overwriting a later report on the same card.
Flags include the client build and exact example/source-record identifiers when available.
The shared backend adds open-to-fixed resolution fields while retaining all historical evidence.

entries.summary: Flags now identify their exact release and JSTA is a dedicated audit account
detail: French flags include the immutable release, run, content and layer provenance available at the time of review.
JSTA receives the same information and flagging controls as JST while keeping separate progress.
Choose your own remembers contributing artists as well as exact song IDs through the shared SongSets backend contract.

entries.summary: The existing Fluency app surface now runs against the clean release architecture
detail: The interface and active-set experience are transplanted from the existing app.
French data is mounted from one explicitly active immutable release.
No historical French sentences or WSD assignments are bundled in the code repository.
